proposed_value: DNA library preparation for ExP STARR-seq involves synthesizing 264 bp enhancer and promoter sequences in an oligonucleotide pool, PCR amplifying them separately, and inserting them into the hSTARR-seq_SCP1 vector using a single pooled Gibson assembly step to generate all pairwise combinations. The vector includes four polyA sequences upstream of the promoter and splice sites upstream of the enhancer to prevent spurious transcription and enable specific cDNA amplification. A 16-mer random barcode is inserted immediately upstream of the enhancer to serve as a plasmid barcode for mRNA origin tracking. After transfection into K562 cells, DNA and RNA are extracted, and libraries are prepared by PCR amplification of cDNA using a primer targeting the splice junction to enrich for reporter mRNA. DNA libraries are generated from input plasmid DNA. Both libraries are sequenced on Illumina platforms to depths of at least 2.6 billion (RNA) and 470 million (DNA) reads per replicate.
rationale:
- DNA library preparation uses PCR-amplified enhancer and promoter sequences cloned into the hSTARR-seq_SCP1 vector via Gibson assembly to generate all pairwise combinations (Passage 7).
- The vector includes splice sites upstream of the enhancer to allow specific amplification of cDNA from reporter mRNA using a splice junction primer, avoiding plasmid DNA amplification (Passage 7).
- A 16-mer barcode is inserted upstream of the enhancer to track mRNA origin, and both DNA and RNA libraries are sequenced to high depth (≥2.6 billion RNA reads, ≥470 million DNA reads) (Passage 2, 9).
